text:
acme-netops: Hey team — after last night's scheduled cert rotation our private endpoint (api.acme.internal) started failing for several client apps. Errors are 'x509: certificate signed by unknown authority' and some clients report cert chain validation failure. Impacting multiple regions in our VPCs. Anyone seen this after a rotation?

maria-support: Sorry to hear that — can you paste the output of `openssl s_client -showcerts -connect api.acme.internal:443 -servername api.acme.internal` or `curl -v`? Also: do you have TLS inspection / proxy on the egress path?

acme-netops: Pasted extract below (sanitized). We *do* have an inline proxy that was upgraded 1h before failures. The `openssl` output shows the server presenting only the leaf cert and a root; the intermediate looks missing/replaced.

```
Certificate chain
 0 s:/CN=api.acme.internal
   i:/CN=Intercept-CA
-----BEGIN CERTIFICATE-----
MIIF... (leaf)
-----END CERTIFICATE-----
 1 s:/CN=Intercept-CA
   i:/CN=Acme Root CA
-----BEGIN CERTIFICATE-----
MIIF... (proxy intercept CA)
-----END CERTIFICATE-----
---
verify error:num=20:unable to get local issuer certificate
```

acme-netops: curl --verbose shows similar: `* SSL peer certificate or SSH remote key was not OK` and reports chain length 2.

maria-support: That output strongly suggests the edge proxy is doing TLS MITM (Intercept-CA). Our rotator uploaded the full chain (leaf -> intermediate -> root) at 2024-06-01T01:45Z. Can you confirm whether the proxy is configured to substitute the intermediate?

cert-rotator-bot: rotation completed for tenant `acme` at 2024-06-01T01:45:12Z, bundle id `v20240601-3`, chain uploaded: [leaf.pem, intermediate-acme.pem, root.pem], bundle-size: 3 certs.

vincent-eng: Looking at the logs it seems our bundle was correct. The proxy is replacing the chain with its own intercept cert (Intercept-CA) — that breaks any client-side pinning or validation expecting Acme intermediate. Two paths: 
1) Customer side: whitelist traffic to avoid TLS inspection for `api.acme.internal` (fastest)
2) Redwood: we can alter rotator to also include the proxy's cross-signed intermediate *if* customer provides it, or include both the CA and cross-signed intermediates when we detect downstream rewriting (longer).

alice-sre: Quick repro steps we asked acme to run and they confirmed: 
- `openssl s_client -showcerts -connect api.acme.internal:443 -servername api.acme.internal` -> shows intercept CA as issuer
- `curl --cacert intermediate-acme.pem https://api.acme.internal` still fails because the presented chain doesn't include the Acme intermediate.

maria-support: For immediate mitigation please ask your infra team to bypass TLS inspection for the Redwood endpoints (SNI `api.acme.internal`) or add our root/intermediate to the proxy truststore so substitution won't be necessary. Customer confirmed bypass fixed the client apps in ~10 minutes.

acme-netops: Confirmed. Bypassing TLS inspection fixed all failing clients. We want a long-term approach because we can't disable inspection for everything.

vincent-eng: Action items: 
- ENG: add optional support in rotator to include multiple intermediate variants (cross-signed) when provided by the customer — tracked in ENG-4521.
- SRE: add a KB note explaining how TLS-inspecting proxies can cause chain mismatches and recommended config (whitelist SNI or import our intermediate into proxy truststore).
- SUPPORT: send customer step-by-step rollback/mitigation doc and follow up with their infra team to coordinate a safe whitelist.

alice-sre: I've opened internal ticket SUPPORT-2309 and linked ENG-4521. Logged root cause as "edge TLS inspection replacing intermediate cert, causing client-side chain verification failures post-rotation."

maria-support: Closing loop — customer will work with their proxy vendor to either add our intermediate to the truststore or create a hostname bypass. We're scheduling engineering work to make rotator more tolerant in cases where middleboxes rewrite chains. :white_check_mark:

acme-netops: Thanks everyone — appreciate the quick triage. Will keep you posted if any regressions appear.
